transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hi, Dr. Smith. It's just... when I start eating, especially at night, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating anymore. It's gotten really overwhelming and I don't know what to do.
Do you feel a loss of control during these nighttime eating episodes, like you can't stop eating even when you want to?

Yes, definitely. Once I start snacking at my desk, it's like a switch flips and I just keep shoving food in my mouth even while I'm telling myself to stop. I only really come out of it when I feel painfully full and sick and realize there are wrappers and containers all over my bed and floor.
Do these episodes only happen at night, or do you have similar loss-of-control eating at other times of the day?

They mostly happen late at night, especially when I'm staying up late to study, code, or stress over school assignments. During the day I might eat irregularly, but it's really at night when the urge to snack spirals into completely losing control.
Do you ever wake up during the night and eat while only partially awake, without full awareness of what you're doing?
No, I'm fully awake when it happens. I'm usually up late studying, coding, or watching videos at my desk, so I'm completely aware of what I'm doing, even though I can't seem to stop myself.
Do you ever eat large amounts of food after your evening meal, even if you're not hungry, and feel distressed about it afterward?

Yes, absolutely. Even if I'm not hungry, I'll end up eating two entire fast-food meals, a huge bag of chips, and half a box of cereal in about an hour while sitting at my desk. Afterward, I feel incredibly guilty, distressed, and physically sick looking at all the empty wrappers.

There is no evidence of sleepwalking or automatism, which rules out sleep-related eating disorder, and the behavior is not better explained by bulimia nervosa or binge eating disorder due to its distinct circadian pattern. Therefore, the candidate list remains unchanged.
